text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A test case is looming on the Federal Government's new anti-strike laws, prompted by an unprecedented request by Coal and Allied, a CRA subsidiary,, for an order prohibiting future industrial action at its Hunter valley No 1 mine. If CRA's application suceeds, it will hand employers a potent and ongoing weapon against illegal stoppages. Page 3.

According to David Lindsay, the assistant manager of Namoi Cotton Co-operative - one of the biggest marketers and processors in the area along the Namoi River in north-west New South Wales - there had been little direct damage to this season's anticipated record cotton crop from severe flooding in the region. Page 3.

According to a secret National Crime Authority report on the Japanese mafia - known as boryokudan or yakuza - members of the boryokudan organised crime syndicate tried to take over one of Australia's premier casinos in Canberra. The report also warns that as much as A$7.7 billion may be laundered through Australia each year. Page 5.

The National Competition Council yesterday approved the first regime for private sector access to part of the proposed national gas grid, recommending certification of a New South Wales access grid. The NCC approval further increases Australia's chances o creating a fully competitive A$6 million national gas market. Page 5. --
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge's proposal for "constitutional surgery" to allow voters to select and sack judges in a referendum, this year's Council of Australian Governments meeting will discuss reforming the High Court, with support from theNorthern Territory, New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, Queensland and Western Australia. Page 1.

ABC chairman Donald McDonald is to seek further explanation from his manager Brian Johns over the national broadcaster's screening of the first of the ACTU-sponsored Whitlam lectures, which Communications Minister Richard Alston described as able to be costrued as a one-off promotion for the Australian Labor Party. Page 1.

Ronald Henry Thomas, the murderer at the centre of the Arnott's biscuits extortion threat who was jailed for life for the fatal shooting of a couple in 1991, has denied any involvement with the extortionists and yesterday appealed for an end to the 17-dayordeal, saying innocent people could be harmed. Page 1.

While indicating yesterday official interest rates were on hold "for the time being", the Reserve Bank criticised Australia's big banks for delaying interest rate cuts by up to 58 days while hitting borrowers with rate rises within 16 days. The central bak was particularly critical of an average delay of six to seven weeks in passing on last year's official rate cuts to mortgages. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following a move by the New South Wales Education Department to reopen investigations into 55 or 56 cases which had not been properly investigated or dealt with when first raised, School Education Director-General Ken Boston admitted yesterday schools had failed to protect students from improper conduct by teachers, and that some allegations had been deliberately covered up by officials. Page 1.

The High Court is under sustained attack from conservative States following its controversial Wik ruling, with Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett requesting that the High Court be made a key agenda at a Premier's meeting in Melbourne next month, where he willrevive plans for a formal consultative role for the States in judicial appointments. Page 1.

In a statement issued through his lawyers, Ronald Henry Thomas, the man at the centre of the Arnott's extortion bid, called on the extortionists to withdraw their demand that four Sydney police officers who gave evidence at his murder trial be forced to udertake lie detection tests. Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston has written to ABC chairman Donald McDonald asking him to explain whether by agreeing to televise the ACTU-funded Whitlam Lecture at the request of ACTU secretary Bill Kelty, it had breached both the ABC Act and its wn editorial guidelines. Page 1.
THE AGE

In a case which echoes the Hindmarsh Island development protest in South Australia, a group of Wathaurong Aborigines have lodged a cultural claim over the proposed new chemical depot site at Point Lillias, raising the prospect of an inquiry and further deays in the relocation of chemical storage from Coode Island. Page 1.

Australian Education Union Victorian president Peter Lord said yesterday many of the State's 1,700 State schools - primary and secondary - face disruption or closure tomorrow when up to 7,000 teachers are expected to attend a strike meeting at the Sports nd Entertainment Centre to protest over education cuts. Page 1.

In a writ lodged in the County Court and served this week on Momentum Films, David Hirschfelder, the composer and producer whose musical score for the internationally successful Australian film Shine earned him an Oscar nomination, is claiming A$200,000 fr royalties from the sales of the soundtrack recording. Page 1.

According to documents obtained by The Age, Civil Aviation Safety Authority chairman Justice Bell Fisher wrote to Transport Minister John Sharp and assured him there were no problems with Airlines of Tasmania, just seven days before the airline was deemedto have serious safety faults and was suspended from flying on February 14. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
